{{Short description|Theorem in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], particularly [[functional analysis]], '''James's theorem''', named for [[Robert C. James]], states that a [[Banach space]] <math>X</math> is [[reflexive space|reflexive]] if and only if every [[Continuous function|continuous]] [[linear functional]]'s [[Dual norm|norm]] on <math>X</math> attains its [[supremum]] on the closed [[unit ball]] in <math>X.</math>

A stronger version of the theorem states that a [[weakly closed]] subset <math>C</math> of a Banach space <math>X</math> is [[Weak topology|weakly compact]] if and only if the [[dual norm]] each continuous linear functional on <math>X</math> attains a maximum on <math>C.</math>

The hypothesis of completeness in the theorem cannot be dropped.<ref>{{harvtxt|James|1971}}</ref>

==Statements==

The space <math>X</math> considered can be a real or complex Banach <span lang="en" dir="ltr">space</span>. Its [[continuous dual space]] is denoted by <math>X^{\prime}.</math> The topological dual of <math>\mathbb{R}</math>-Banach space deduced from <math>X</math> by any restriction scalar will be denoted <math>X^{\prime}_{\R}.</math> (It is of interest only if <math>X</math> is a complex space because if <math>X</math> is a <math>\R</math>-space then <math>X^{\prime}_{\R} = X^{\prime}.</math>)

{{math theorem|name=James compactness criterion|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a Banach space and <math>A</math> a weakly closed nonempty subset of <math>X.</math> The following conditions are equivalent:
* <math>A</math> is weakly compact.
* For every <math>f \in X^{\prime},</math> there exists an element <math>a_0 \in A</math> such that <math>\left|f\left(a_0\right)\right| = \sup_{a \in A} |f(a)|.</math>
* For any <math>f \in X^{\prime}_{\R},</math> there exists an element <math>a_0 \in A</math> such that <math>f\left(a_0\right) = \sup_{a \in A} |f(a)|.</math>
* For any <math>f \in X^{\prime}_{\R},</math> there exists an element <math>a_0 \in A</math> such that <math>f\left(a_0\right) = \sup_{a \in A} f(a).</math>
}}

A Banach space being reflexive if and only if its closed unit ball is weakly compact one deduces from this, since the norm of a continuous linear form is the upper bound of its modulus on this ball:

{{math theorem|name=James's theorem|note=|style=|math_statement=
A Banach space <math>X</math> is reflexive if and only if for all <math>f \in X^{\prime},</math> there exists an element <math>a \in X</math> of norm <math>\|a\| \leq 1</math> such that <math>f(a) = \|f\|.</math>
}}

==History==

Historically, these sentences were proved in reverse order. In 1957, James had proved the reflexivity criterion for separable Banach spaces<ref>{{harvtxt|James|1957}}</ref> and 1964 for general Banach spaces.<ref>{{harvtxt|James|1964}}</ref> Since the reflexivity is equivalent to the weak compactness of the unit sphere, Victor L. Klee reformulated this as a compactness criterion for the unit sphere in 1962 and assumes that this criterion characterizes any weakly compact quantities.<ref>{{harvtxt|Klee|1962}}</ref> This was then actually proved by James in 1964.<ref>{{harvtxt|James|1964}}</ref>
